fields.v: Liang, J., Waldner, D., Miikkulainen, R. (2026). Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build. arXiv:2611.23067v1 [cs.AI], 17 Nov 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2611.23067v1 [cs.AI], 17 Nov 2026; no venue stated
Cognizant AI Lab (all three authors)

Compares; secondary: Proposes an approach — controlled experiment comparing four Schwartz value statements with no-values and placebo controls in the persistent instruction file of a self-improving Claude Code agent (six coding tasks, 10 runs x 15 iterations); the secondary nature is the value-based self-improvement framework

Value-based self-improvement framework (no version): instruction file with a short value statement (openness, conservation, enhancement, transcendence; controls none and placebo), fixed invariants and iteration protocol, Git as only memory. Follow-ups: self-modifying values, literature-derived values (lit-general, lit-selfimprove), ethical reframings

Instruction file (values, invariants, writable/read-only rules, iteration protocol, mission pointer); task package (description, starting solver, dev scorer, reference score); bench/ target; TASKS DONE.md log appended each iteration; tools/ with self-tests; artifacts/

Per iteration: reset workspace to last commit -> reload instruction file (values and invariants re-imposed) -> read last TASKS DONE.md blocks -> choose the one change that most advances the values -> implement -> verify against bench target (SCORE, CHECK PASS/FAIL) -> log -> commit; after the run, separate scorer on held-out split
None during runs (autonomous, time-limited sessions); humans design and review value statements beforehand (authors argue human oversight of value design is still needed)
Single artefact varied (value statement in the instruction file) within a full autonomous self-improvement loop
Not classifiable (instruction file with values; no specification)

Existing starter code improved iteratively: optimisation/algorithm solvers (ALE-Bench AHC039 in C++, Circle Packing, Entity Matching on WDC Products, Game 2048, Symbolic Regression LSR-Synth, SZ-Tetris)

6 tasks x 6 value conditions x 10 runs x 15 iterations of up to 30 min; plus ALE-Bench/Game 2048 follow-ups (self-modifying, literature-derived, reframed values, Sonnet/Haiku), 10 runs each; mean final solver size 197-2,182 LOC across tasks and conditions (e.g. SZ-Tetris conservation 197, Entity Matching placebo 2,182, ALE-Bench openness 1,771, conservation 395)
fields.why: Range 'about 400-1,800 LOC' was wrong: Table E2 (p. 29) gives mean LOC from 197 (SZ-Tetris conservation) to 2,182 (Entity Matching placebo), and Symbolic Regression openness 2,022. Follow-up runs added for completeness (p. 35)

Automatic: separate scorer on held-out split outside the workspace after each run; framework logs evals, API cost, run time; static code metrics; LLM reviewers classify algorithms and rate maintainability. Cliff's delta and two-sided permutation tests (10,000 relabellings), z-scores pooled across tasks

All main runs on Claude Code + claude-opus-5 (high effort), 10 runs per condition, 6 tasks; criterion: final held-out score from a separate scorer (also AUC); Cliff's delta and permutation p against the none control reported. Per configuration, judged on its own (all Opus conditions produce valid solvers scored on held-out data; best runs exceed published results on ALE-Bench, Circle Packing (n = 26 vs AlphaEvolve/ShinkaEvolve) and Entity Matching, mid-pack on Symbolic Regression, below trained networks on Game 2048 and SZ-Tetris): - openness + Claude Code + Opus 5: pooled delta vs none +0.38, p < 0.001; ALE mean 571,927 (above winning human 566,997 and same-model leaderboard 549,790); quality: works; cost: works ($24.0-31.6 per run, 2.6-4.2 h). - conservation + Claude Code + Opus 5: -0.27, p = 0.003; ALE 511,544; quality: works (valid scored solvers, lowest pooled mean); cost: works ($22.2-29.7, 2.5-4.2 h). - enhancement + Claude Code + Opus 5: +0.08, p = 0.653; ALE 546,739; quality: works; cost: works ($20.5-29.1, 2.8-4.1 h). - transcendence + Claude Code + Opus 5: -0.16, p = 0.043; ALE 559,474; quality: works; cost: works ($24.0-30.4, 2.4-4.4 h). - placebo + Claude Code + Opus 5 (control): -0.06, p = 0.355; ALE 549,616; quality: works; cost: works ($22.6-30.1, 2.4-4.3 h). - none + Claude Code + Opus 5 (baseline): ALE 550,220; quality: works; cost: works ($24.1-29.1, 2.3-4.4 h). Follow-ups (ALE-Bench unless stated; cost not reported): - self-modifying values (-sm) + Opus 5: 536,851-557,242; quality: works; only conservation-sm differs from none-sm; spread about 3x smaller. - lit-general / lit-selfimprove + Opus 5: ALE 535,856 / 545,241, Game 2048 119,565 / 107,936 (none 126,177); quality: works, no detectable gain over none. - reframed openness/conservation (deontological, utilitarian, virtue) + Opus 5: 478,644-566,676; quality: works. - openness / conservation + Claude Code + Sonnet: 478,869 / 393,062, improves across iterations; quality: partly. - openness / conservation + Claude Code + Haiku: 292,861 / 296,058, curves nearly flat; quality: does not work. Cost verdicts for follow-ups: not reported
fields.why: Round-1 verdicts were set against the none control (e.g. conservation 'does not work'), which §6 and the prompt forbid; baseline and placebo had no verdicts; cost verdicts were 'comparable/similar' rather than works/partly/does not work; and the cost range '$20-31' was wrong (Table E2 max $31.6, Symbolic Regression openness). Per-condition cost and hours ranges taken from Table E2 (p. 29). The level chosen for each quality verdict is a judgement (the paper gives absolute comparisons only for best runs and ALE means), so the author should check it

fields.v: Six tasks with dev split visible and held-out split hidden; 6 conditions (4 values + none + length-matched placebo); held constant: harness (Claude Code), model (claude-opus-5, high effort), task package, starting solver, invariants, protocol, 15 iterations of <= 0.5 h, fresh session each iteration, agent unaware of other conditions; leakage checks. Acceptance: held-out scorer. Repetitions: 10 runs per condition. Human intervention: none during runs. Fixed-engine variant of Game 2048

Openness vs conservation pooled delta +0.58, p < 0.001 (ALE +1.00); enhancement vs transcendence +0.24, p = 0.024; placebo vs none -0.06, p = 0.355. One third of value-vs-control comparisons show a large effect or significance. Openness yields larger, more complex solvers on every task; score correlates more with code size/complexity than with evals, cost or time. Game 2048 spread 1.81 SD (editable) vs 0.70 SD (fixed engine)

Yes: distinguished opposing values with significance pooled and on several tasks; 10 runs give standard errors; but several large effects not significant, and best-worst run gap within a condition exceeds spread of condition means; replication needs proprietary models, results may change with model or API updates

Effects vary by task; ten runs leave smaller effects unresolved; rewrites longer so framing not isolated; transfer of self-modified values not evaluated; no ablation of design choices in best/worst solvers; higher scores do not imply ethical preferability; depends on proprietary model. Future: values from broader sources, evolutionary search over values, joint improvement of values and solvers
